drivingQuestion: Where does R' Yoḥanan's permission of a basket-covering apply?
outcomeNote: Abaye (or Rav Kahana) locates the ruling in semi-private passageways

segments.he: קַלְתָּהּ שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי, דָּת יְהוּדִית — אֲפִילּוּ קַלְתָּהּ נָמֵי אָסוּר.
segments.en: if she covers her head with «her basket» [«kilta»], «it seems well» and is sufficient. But by «precepts of Jewish» women, i.e., custom, «even» if her head is covered by «her basket» this «is also prohibited;» she requires a substantial head covering.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קַלְתָּהּ, אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם פְּרוּעַ רֹאשׁ. הָוֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: הֵיכָא? אִילֵּימָא בְּשׁוּק — דָּת יְהוּדִית הִיא! וְאֶלָּא בֶּחָצֵר — אִם כֵּן לֹא הִנַּחְתָּ בַּת לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁיּוֹשֶׁבֶת תַּחַת בַּעְלָהּ! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב כָּהֲנָא: מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר וְדֶרֶךְ מָבוֹי.
segments.en: «Rabbi Asi said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» If she covers her head with «her basket, there is no» violation of the prohibition against having «an uncovered head. Rabbi Zeira discussed it: Where» is the woman that Rabbi Yoḥanan is referring to? «If we say» he means that she appears this way «in the marketplace, this is» a violation of «precepts of Jewish» women, as explained previously. «And» if you say «rather» that he means she appears this way «in» her own «courtyard, if so, you have not allowed» any «daughter of our father Abraham to remain with her husband,» since most women are not careful to cover their heads completely inside their own courtyards. «Abaye said, and some say that Rav Kahana» said: Rabbi Yoḥanan is referring to when she walks «from» one «courtyard to» another «courtyard or via an alleyway.» Although these places are not considered public areas, strangers may still be present in them.
